newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank to help fund India tuberculosis fight.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to help fund India tuberculosis fight.

text.p: The World Bank said on Friday it had approved a $142.4 million, low-interest loan to combat tuberculosis (TB) in India, where 500,000 people die each year from the disease.

The Washington-based development bank said in a statement that the loan -- the biggest ever in the global fight against the lung disease -- would fund a path-breaking programme to treat three million TB cases over five years.

If the target of an 85-percent cure rate is achieved, at least 1.5 million TB patients will be cured, it said. After the second year of the project, India will prevent about 140,000 TB-related deaths every year, it said.
Some 2.9 million people die from TB every year worldwide, about one fifth of them in India. An estimated 26 percent of all deaths among adults aged 15 to 59 is due to TB, the bank said.
More than 1.2 million TB cases are reported in India every year, and up to half the population is infected, it said.

The World Bank's concessional lending arm, the International Development Association, will provide a $142.4 million credit, repayable over 35 years. The Indian government will contribute $34 million towards the project, which will be based on sputum analysis rather than ordinary X-ray.
